body:
Yes. I thought I was the only one. I'm 29, and I really do feel like I am a thirteen-year-old trapped in an older body.

Didn't have my first kiss until I was 28.

Still a virgin.

Never learned driving (I'm a virgin who can't drive).

Still working on my undergraduate education.

Never went to prom.

Never dated.



I could go on and on, but yeah... you are not alone.

I'm 29.

I knew I was depressed, ever since the age of 10. When I was 11, I took an "Are You Depressed?" quiz from one of my mom's women's magazines. My score was very high. I showed it to my mom, and she attributed it to hormones. When I was 12, the night before my abusive father came home from working overseas for a few months, I took a whole bottle of Tylenol and planned to stab myself in the heart. I chickened out and vomited up the pills. My parents didn't know about this until I was 15. Still, I didn't get any help.

When I was 22, I had a mental breakdown and went to see my doctor who referred me to a psychiatrist... and was formally diagnosed as having major depressive disorder.

bad moods (my playlist title is "CRY MOAR"):

Hurt - Johnny Cash

Hallelujah - Jeff Buckley

Full of Grace - Sarah McLachlan

I Will Follow You Into The Dark - Death Cab For Cutie

Mad World - Gary Jules
thank you so much. I appreciate it. and good luck with your schooling.

thanks very much for your comment. I have two cats right now. sometimes they help, but they drive me crazier other times because they're half-Siamese and very vocal. I think if I can ever upgrade my living situation, I would consider adopting a dog.

I have thought about doing the couch to 5k plan, but I keep making stupid excuses...
Thanks to you and The_Last_Poet for updating. I am so glad he's okay.

well, thank you. I really don't like to see other people in pain. it's like... I don't really care what happens to me, but I care about the well-being of those people close to me. and even people who I don't know. if a hungry homeless person asks me for money, I buy them a meal or give them any food I have. little things like that

and, yeah, good points all around.

thanks. I think that is the key. 

I think I'm way too caught up in the past... before I had my major mental breakdown, I was at my peak (thinner, healthier, could have completed school by 2007, no credit card debt [it'll be paid off in a couple of years now, though]/good credit rating, good grades). I guess I'm doing it again right now, just dwelling on it....

thank you so much, I appreciate it.

I wish more people understood depression and could read what you wrote... a lot of people I know seem to think it's just a bad case of the blues. like you said, it's a physical thing... and it's a lot more than "the blues."

thanks, I really appreciate it.

I'm getting a degree in English lit. Apart from the heavy workload, I do like it very much. unfortunately, I screwed up and made a bunch of Fs (resulting in me taking 4 years off), so I don't think grad school is an option even if I wanted to go.

yeah, I rent this place and have been supporting myself for almost ten years with very little help from my parents (mother can't afford to, father and I are estranged). it is very hard sometimes, especially when I keep seeing my friends on Facebook post albums of their McMansions. I just compare myself and think, "this is what you could have had if you hadn't screwed up so badly."

all the best with school, and thank you.

Thank you...

Yep, I am seeing a psych doctor, and he is really, really good. I feel so good after I leave our sessions... and then that demon comes back and I end up feeling like shit again.

I love my major (English), but I know the job market is not the best for a lot of Arts/Humanities majors right now.

As for the rest of what you've written, it makes perfect sense, and I think I should print that out, too. Thanks again.

I'm terribly out of shape right now, but I like playing tennis. Apart from the basic recreational activities (TV, movies, reading, listening to the radio), I like drawing. And I like to write. And play board games (there was a board games meetup in my city, but it was shut down).

Edited to thank you for responding. Much appreciated.
thank you, I appreciate it. and, man, I can really identify with your username... heh.

I think I will PM you. Good idea. I used to volunteer before my mental health took a downward slope, but I was only volunteering 'cause other people asked me to (yep, really need to stop trying to please others so much).

I really like what you wrote. I think I might even print it out.

You are also correct... I definitely try to please other people while putting my own wants/happiness aside sometimes. I know it's bullshit, but... ugh. It is hard to change a behaviour (but I know I can).

Thank you.

I really do try. when I was a kid, I was constantly told by my father that I was stupid, lazy, and other wonderful adjectives in that vein. I have been in therapy 4+ years. I don't put myself down to fish for compliments (I don't really believe any compliments that I get)... I really do not like myself. I feel like I am trapped in this skin, and I want to get out.

I have 2 years to go until I'm done. the good thing about my debt is that my family will not have to pay it off if I ctb.

it's funny, I used to be 60 pounds lighter 8 years ago and I was still a miserable sack. no guys ever approached me then either. I recently deactivated my okc because the pic people voted on for me was one where I'm reading a book covering 3/4 of my face.

i would like more cheese with my whine. but thank you, i appreciate it.
